description:
Problem: when evaluate() raises (API, fetch or policy errors), main() in _project/scripts/oracle_gate.py returns ERROR without posting. Any earlier oracle-gate success on the head therefore stays. The hourly sweep in oracle-gate.yml also lists at most 200 open develop pull requests (gh pr list --limit 200) within a 15-minute timeout. The sweep is not a bound on how long a stale success can stand.

Outcome: when the pull request's head SHA is known and evaluation then fails, the gate posts failure with a short error description on that head. When the head cannot be read at all, nothing is posted, which is the documented limit. The sweep covers every open develop pull request, not just the first 200.

Decision gates (stop and report if one fails):
1. A pull request whose base is not develop (UngatedBase) must still post nothing; an evaluation error must not post for it either.
2. Blast radius: an API outage would turn open pull requests to failure until their next evaluation. That is the intended fail-closed trade-off. Record it in the design doc. If repository policy forbids it, stop.
3. Keep the decision rule unchanged: only the error path changes.

Item guardrails: no change to decide() or the App binding. Posting still uses only the App token. --no-post never posts. The sweep keeps per-PR error aggregation and still exits non-zero when any pull request errored.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Close out with make pr-preflight, make pr-open, oracle SHIP on the exact head, then make pr-arm. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings (COMMENT-POLICY-001). Every behavior change gets a test that fails on the previous code.
